The co-stardom network can be represented by an undirected graph of nodes and links.  Nodes correspond to the movie star actors and two nodes are linked if they co-starred (performed) in the same movie.  The links are un-directed, and can be weighted or not depending on the goals of study.  If the number of times two actors appeared in a movie is needed, links are assigned weights.  The co-stardom network can also be represented by a bipartite graph where nodes are of two types: actors and movies.  And edges connect different types of nodes (i.e. actors to movies) if they have a relationship (actors in a movie).  Initially the network was found to have a small-world property.  Afterwards, it was discovered that it exhibits a scale-free (power-law) behavior.
